draft.title: Organising ideas for a purpose
card: Authors choose the order of their ideas to suit their purpose. The same ideas in a different order can have a different effect on a reader.
One common plan is to answer an objection before the reader raises it. The author states the opposing view, then replies to it, so the reader has fewer reasons to disagree.
Authors link ideas with connecting words and phrases, such as however, because, as a result and for example. These show how one idea relates to the next.
Readers judge how well the order works. They ask whether it helps the author achieve their purpose, such as persuading, explaining or entertaining.
draft.remember: Order and links are choices. Judge them by whether they help the purpose.

a.q: A writer argues that schools should start later. Before giving her own reasons, she admits that later starts may upset bus timetables, then explains how they could be changed. Why does she order her ideas this way?
opts: To answer a likely objection before the reader raises it
To show that she has no strong view on the topic
To entertain the reader with a surprising story first
To list her reasons from the weakest to the strongest
a.why: She states the problem a reader might raise and then replies to it. This makes the argument harder to doubt. It does not show a lack of view, because she still argues for later starts.
a.clue: Think about what the reader might say against her view.

b.q: Dev writes a speech urging students to join a beach clean-up. He opens with a short story about a turtle hurt by litter, then gives facts, then says how to sign up. Which comment best judges how well this order suits his purpose?
opts: It works: the story gains interest, then facts and a next step
It fails: a story must come after the facts in any speech
It works: every speech is best when it opens with a story
It fails: the sign-up details must be placed before the facts
b.why: His purpose is to persuade students to act. The story gains attention, the facts support it, and the sign-up gives a next step. The second option is wrong because no order is right in every text. Judging means linking the order to the purpose.
b.clue: Match each step of the speech to what he wants the audience to do.
